text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in daily KAUPPALEHTI this morning. Other papers were not published due to public holiday on Monday.
- The government is expected to propose tighter legislation against insider trading this spring. According to a draft proposal, the maximum prison sentence would rise to four years from two.
- Finnish industrial production to grow by an average of four percent towards the end of the decade, The Research Insitute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) forecasts.
- Cooperative banking group and OKOBANK CEO Antti Tanskanen expects more mergers in the banking sector. Also says planned 150,000 markka limit on government deposit quarantees is too low.
